title: Fascism and Nazism

cards.h: How a dictator was handed power by people who thought they could control him
cards.b:
On 30 January 1933, the German president Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler as chancellor. Conservative politicians thought they could use him and keep him in check.

Within 18 months he had no checks left.

Fascism began in Italy. Mussolini, once a socialist, led his Blackshirts in the 'March on Rome' (October 1922). The king asked him to form a government. By 1925 he had made himself dictator.

Fascists glorified the nation, the leader and violence, and hated democracy, liberals and socialists.

After a failed coup in 1923, Hitler turned to elections. The Nazis won 37 percent in July 1932, their best free result. After the Reichstag fire (February 1933) and the Enabling Act (March 1933), Germany became a one-party dictatorship.

The Nazis claimed 'Aryans' were a master race. They stripped Jews of citizenship and rights with the Nuremberg Laws (1935). On 9-10 November 1938 came Kristallnacht, when synagogues and Jewish shops were smashed and about 30,000 Jewish men arrested.

Hitler's regime also persecuted Roma, disabled people, homosexuals and political opponents.

Reasons historians give: economic misery, anger over Versailles, fear of communism, weak democratic habits, clever propaganda by Joseph Goebbels, and violence by the SA. The Nazi state also gave many Germans jobs and national pride.

But the same state was a machine of terror, with the Gestapo, camps and no free press.

Myth: Germans voted him in as dictator.Fact: the Nazis never won a majority in a free election. In November 1932 their share fell to about 33 percent. Hindenburg and conservative politicians appointed Hitler chancellor. He then used emergency powers to destroy democracy.

It shows how fragile democracy can be when elites bargain with extremists.

Five things to remember

  1. Mussolini took power in 1922.
  2. Hitler was appointed in January 1933.
  3. The Enabling Act ended democracy.
  4. Nuremberg Laws and Kristallnacht targeted Jews.
  5. Bose, Gandhi and Nehru reacted differently.

Think about it

  • How can democracies protect themselves?
  • Why did people support or tolerate the regime?
